logicalCoherence.rationale: The absorption critique is coherent, but its inference from later compensation to the abuser's necessary providential instrumentality is not unavoidable.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The concrete abuse case powerfully tests the general defense, though one cited interlocutor's formulation may not establish every version of theism.

relevanceWithinTier.rationale: Within the central counterevidence tier, it directly tests whether the affirmative's redemption answer can discriminate justified permission from arbitrary horror.

con-providential-absorption-of-horror.evidenceBasis: Hitchens applies a prolonged incest and captivity case to the claim that God will compensate suffering and argues this risks making the abuser providentially instrumental.
